title: Momentary Awareness Check-in
opening: At a suitable transition, briefly notice what is present, identify anything that matters to the next activity, and continue.

labels.before: You have just left a tense call. Before replying to a colleague, notice what you carry into the next conversation.
labels.thoughtValue: A line from the earlier call is still repeating in your mind.
labels.surroundingsValue: The colleague's message asks for the draft by noon.
labels.observation: What you can observe: the message asks for the draft by noon.
labels.interpretation: A possible story: “They think I am unreliable.” The message does not establish that meaning.
labels.continue: The noon deadline affects the next action. The irritation is also present, but it does not tell you what the colleague intended.
labels.nextAction: Check whether the draft can be sent by noon, then reply with the actual timing. You could choose differently if the deadline is unsafe or impossible.
labels.notRequired: Noticing does not require changing the feeling or analyzing every thought. A clear next step, a safety demand or no useful pause can be a reason to continue without this check-in.
labels.practiceIntro: At one suitable transition, name one internal condition and one external condition. Then note what, if anything, affects the next activity.
labels.nextPrompt: What matters to the next activity, and what will you continue with? If nothing changes, write “No change.”
labels.privacy: This reflection is private to you. Saving it does not mark the lesson complete or assess what you noticed.
labels.sourceQuote: At a transition, pause and ask, “What is awareness noticing right now?” Include sensations, thoughts, feelings and surroundings, then continue the activity.

source.assessmentPolicy: Open-ended responses have no stored gold answer. The exact source definition is the practice-card answer only.
